text:
Based on the retrieved passages, recovery of the $18,000 markdown appears unlikely, though no final ruling on this specific claim is in the record.

The shipper's original demand explicitly included this cost: "Our current demand is $29,920.00, consisting of product shortage/damage, inspection and rework costs, the commercial markdown caused by the missed promotion launch, and a refund of the freight charge." [email_thread] The shipper later detailed it further: "Because they arrived after launch, we incurred an $18,000 markdown to move the inventory. We expect BlueLine to address that delay loss as well." [email_thread]

The carrier, however, has rejected this component. Its stated position is: "Our position is that the service was Standard LTL, not a guaranteed appointment service. The agreement excludes consequential and loss-of-market damages for delay." [email_thread] It confirmed the exclusion directly in its offer: "This offer does not include inspection/repack expense, late-delivery markdown, or freight refund." [email_thread]

A prior case with the same carrier reinforces this outcome. Historical claim HC-2025-0094, also a DELAY claim with "No guaranteed service," resolved with "Promotion markdown denied; commercial freight refund approved." [historical_claims]

The internal claim record's analyst note echoes the same caution for this claim: "Promotion-impact component is commercially important but may not be contractually recoverable." [claim_snapshot]

What's missing to give a definitive answer: the passages do not include the actual carrier service agreement/tariff language on delay and consequential/loss-of-market damages, nor any final settlement, arbitration outcome, or legal determination for this specific claim (FCL-2026-0147) — only the carrier's negotiating position and one historical precedent are available.
